Score Life's Essential 8 cardiovascular health

Source: R/score-le8.R
score_le8.Rd

Computes the eight Life's Essential 8 (LE8) component scores and the composite score using the American Heart Association's 2022 Presidential Advisory. Rows aged 20 years or older are scored with the adult definitions; rows aged 4 months to 19 years are scored with the pediatric definitions. Component scores are calculated wherever sufficient inputs are available, without imputing missing values.

Usage

score_le8(
  data,
  diet_method = "mepa",
  mepa_columns = NULL,
  min_components = 7L,
  dash_columns = NULL,
  dash_cutpoints = NULL,
  hei2015_columns = NULL,
  hei2015_cutpoints = NULL,
  reference = "nhanes_2015_2018",
  impute = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per person (or visit) and the input columns described below. Adults and children may be mixed.

diet_method

A single diet-scoring method applied to every row in data: "mepa" (the default), "dash", "hei2015", or "percentile". Values are matched case-insensitively. Score data that use different methods in separate calls.

mepa_columns

NULL, or a named character vector mapping canonical MEPA fields to columns in data. The names are canonical fields (the 16 screener items, sex, and milk_source) and the values are actual column names. Unmapped fields use their canonical names.

min_components

A single integer from 1 to 8 specifying the minimum number of non-missing LE8 component scores required to calculate le8_composite_score. The default is 7. Available component scores are averaged without imputation, which treats a missing component as equal to the average of the others; observations below the threshold receive NA_real_. Pediatric data usually need a lower value; see Pediatric scoring. To account for missing inputs instead, use impute.

dash_columns, hei2015_columns

NULL, or named character vectors mapping canonical DASH or HEI-2015 fields to columns in data. Unmapped fields default to the canonical name prefixed with dash_ or hei2015_. Names and input column names are matched case-insensitively.

dash_cutpoints

NULL to use the packaged DASH intake quintiles and total-score cutpoints, or a named list containing the eight canonical DASH fields and total. Each intake vector contains four nondecreasing reference quintile cutpoints (20th, 40th, 60th, 80th percentiles), in the same units as the inputs. total contains four nondecreasing reference DASH-total cutpoints (25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles), each from 8 to 40. Tied cutpoints are allowed. Explicit cutpoints bypass reference and use inputs in their supplied units, without energy standardization, preserving existing calls.

hei2015_cutpoints

NULL to use reference, or four nondecreasing reference HEI-2015-total cutpoints (25th, 50th, 75th, 95th percentiles), each from 0 to 100. Tied cutpoints are allowed.

reference

"nhanes_2015_2018" (the default), or a method-matched diet_reference() object. Used for already-computed indices and raw intake scoring when explicit cutpoints are absent. Raw DASH requires the packaged reference's intake quintiles; for other DASH definitions, supply dash_cutpoints. Direct percentiles and explicit raw cutpoints bypass reference lookup. The built-in references describe nonpregnant adults aged 20+ with two reliable recalls; they are derived estimates, not AHA-published cutpoints, and are refused for pediatric rows.

impute

Whether to multiply impute missing inputs before scoring: FALSE (the default), TRUE for the default settings, or le8_imputation_control() to set the number of imputations, a seed, auxiliary predictors, and other mice::mice() arguments. Requires the mice package and diet_method = "mepa". See Multiple imputation.

Value

An essential8_scores object: data, with its original class (so tibbles and grouped tibbles are returned as such) and columns, plus mepa_total (items met on the age-appropriate MEPA screener: 0-16 from age 6, 0-10 at ages 2-5, 0-6 at 6-23 months), dash_total, and hei2015_total (missing unless calculated from the corresponding raw inputs), physical_activity_moderate_equivalent_minutes (weekly minutes used for adults and children aged 6+), the eight component scores (diet_score, physical_activity_score, nicotine_score, sleep_score, bmi_score, blood_lipids_score, blood_glucose_score, and blood_pressure_score), n_components, le8_composite_score, le8_complete, le8_category, and le8_population ("adult" or "pediatric"). The component count reports how many scores contributed to the composite score; le8_complete is TRUE only when all eight components are available. Categories are "low" for scores below 50, "moderate" for scores from 50 to less than 80, and "high" for scores of at least 80. The category is missing when the composite score is missing. For raw DASH calls, the eight component scores (1 to 5 points each) are also appended as dash_<field>_score; they sum to dash_total. For raw HEI-2015 calls, the 13 component scores are also appended as hei2015_<component>_score, including fatty_acids and saturated_fats.

With impute, an essential8_imputed_scores object instead: the scored completed data sets stacked, with the imputation number in .imp and the row of data in .id. It is a data frame, or a tibble for tibble input (ungrouped). The mids object from mice is kept as attr(x, "mids") for diagnostics, for example plot(attr(x, "mids")) to check convergence.

data must not already contain any of these output columns (compared case-insensitively), or the le8_-prefixed component names used by essential8 0.3.0 and earlier; rename or remove them first.

The essential8_scores class adds summary(), tidy(), plot(), and dplyr summarise() methods. See as_le8_scores() for when the class is kept and how to restore it.

Diet scoring methods

MEPA retains the individual assessment pathway. For population research, diet_method = "dash" accepts an already-computed index in dash, and diet_method = "hei2015" accepts an already-computed index in hei2015. Either method alternatively accepts a percentile in diet_value (0 to 100). Both methods also calculate raw totals from the intake fields below, using the packaged reference by default. Raw HEI-2015 also accepts a custom diet_reference(); raw DASH supports custom definitions via dash_cutpoints. Do not supply both the index column and an observed percentile; an entirely missing diet_value column is ignored. Data with no diet inputs retain the package's usual missing-component behavior. Once raw scoring is selected, every raw input column must be present (values may be missing); an absent column is an error rather than a silently missing diet score.

An index is compared with fixed reference cutpoints to identify its percentile category. The package does not estimate an exact percentile from four cutpoints, or rank the current cohort against itself. Specify reference = "nhanes_2015_2018" explicitly in reproducible analyses.

The built-in DASH reference is specifically the 8-to-40 Fung-style FPED construction identified as essential8_fung_fped_v1; it requires matching food definitions, pooled weighted intake quintiles, and tie handling. Other DASH definitions need a custom reference. HEI-2015 indices must be constructed using an appropriate established method; the built-in reference uses individual scoring after averaging the same two recalls' constituents and energy. It is not a usual-intake or population-ratio estimate. Both references use NHANES 2015-2016 and 2017-2018, two-day dietary weights divided by two, and the NHANES strata and PSU design. Detailed methodology, source URLs, hashes, sample counts, and index definitions accompany the references and the maintainer script data-raw/build_diet_references.R in the repository.

Fractional inputs confined to 0-1 (other than endpoints alone) are rejected as apparent proportions; supply percentile points, such as 95, not 0.95. This safeguard also rejects a batch consisting only of genuine fractional percentiles below 1. Values are never automatically multiplied by 100.

Supply one input pathway per call: raw intake, a precomputed index, or a percentile. Raw intake fields cannot be combined with a precomputed index or observed percentile. Raw fields are food-group and nutrient summaries, prepared before scoring; the function does not parse dietary-recall files. See vignette("population-diets") for executable examples and units.

Input columns

The column names below are case-sensitive; a name that differs only by case (for example BMI) is an error. MEPA, DASH, and HEI-2015 diet fields are matched case-insensitively. A column whose values are all missing may be logical NA (as read.csv() produces for a blank column). Columns that only apply to adults or only to children are ignored for other rows.

  • age: Age in years; must be present, complete, and at least 4 months (1/3 year). Rows aged 20 or older are scored as adults.

  • age_months: Optional age in months, used for the pediatric age bands when observed. It must fall within the same completed year as age.

  • For diet_method = "mepa", the 16 Table C screener-item columns named below and sex (or female when sex is absent). The same columns serve children; see Pediatric input columns for which items each age uses. The item names are matched exactly after case normalization. If any screener item is present, every field used at the ages in data is required (all 16 items and sex when any row is aged 6 or older); omitting every item leaves the diet component missing. Supply daily servings in olive_oil, green_leafy_vegetables, other_vegetables, and whole_grains; supply weekly servings or frequency in berries, other_fruit, meat, fish, chicken, cheese, butter_cream, beans, sweets_and_pastries, nuts, and alcohol; supply the number of times per week that fast-food meals are consumed in fast_food. Sex may be encoded as "m"/"f", "male"/"female", or 0/1, where 0 is male and 1 is female. Character encodings are matched case-insensitively, and character "0"/"1" values are also accepted. A logical female column (TRUE for female) is also accepted.

  • dash or hei2015: An already-computed index for the selected population diet method. HEI-2015 is bounded by 0 to 100. The built-in DASH reference requires its documented 8-to-40 definition; custom DASH references can specify other index ranges. These columns are unrelated to MEPA.

  • For raw DASH scoring, supply daily intakes in dash_fruits, dash_vegetables, dash_nuts_and_legumes, dash_whole_grains, dash_low_fat_dairy, dash_red_and_processed_meat, and dash_sweetened_beverages; supply sodium in mg/day in dash_sodium. Canonical mapping fields omit the dash_ prefix. Fruits include juice; vegetables exclude potatoes and legumes. Food groups and serving definitions must match the reference. With the packaged reference, also supply positive kcal/day in dash_energy_kcal; sodium is standardized to 2,000 kcal before scoring. Other fields must use the FPED-derived units and definitions in vignette("population-diets"), including fruit cup equivalents, whole-grain ounce equivalents, and the specified vegetable, dairy, protein, and beverage conversions. With explicit dash_cutpoints, energy is not required and no standardization is applied.

  • For raw HEI-2015 scoring, supply hei2015_energy_kcal (positive kcal/day, including alcohol); cup equivalents/day in hei2015_total_fruits, hei2015_whole_fruits, hei2015_total_vegetables, hei2015_greens_and_beans, and hei2015_dairy; ounce equivalents/day in hei2015_whole_grains, hei2015_total_protein_foods, hei2015_seafood_and_plant_proteins, and hei2015_refined_grains; grams/day in hei2015_polyunsaturated_fat, hei2015_monounsaturated_fat, and hei2015_saturated_fat; mg/day in hei2015_sodium; and teaspoon equivalents/day in hei2015_added_sugars. Canonical mapping fields omit the hei2015_ prefix. Food-group totals must already include legumes in both vegetable and protein components as specified by HEI-2015. Total fruits include juice; whole fruits do not.

  • diet_value: A direct percentile for "dash", "hei2015", or the backward-compatible generic "percentile" method. Supply a DASH or HEI-2015 percentile from 0 to 100, calculated against the relevant reference distribution. The function does not rank supplied rows against one another. If this column is absent or missing, the diet score is missing. MEPA and raw-intake calls require it to be absent or entirely missing.

  • moderate_activity_minutes and vigorous_activity_minutes: Weekly minutes. For adults, each vigorous minute counts as two moderate-equivalent minutes; for children aged 6 to 19, every minute counts once.

  • smoking_status: One of "never", "former", or "current". See Pediatric input columns for the pediatric meaning.

  • years_since_quit: Years since quitting combustible tobacco. This is used only for adults whose smoking_status is "former".

  • current_inhaled_nds: Whether an inhaled nicotine-delivery system is currently used.

  • secondhand_smoke_home: Whether the person lives with an active indoor smoker.

  • sleep_hours: Average hours of sleep per night (per 24 hours, including naps, for children aged 5 or younger).

  • bmi: Adult body mass index in kg/m^2. Values below 18.5 are not scored because the AHA advisory defers to clinician judgment for underweight adults.

  • bmi_profile: Either "general" or "asian_pacific" (adults). The function never infers a profile from race or ethnicity.

  • non_hdl_cholesterol: Non-HDL cholesterol in mg/dL.

  • lipid_lowering_treatment: Whether the lipid value is drug treated.

  • diabetes: Whether diabetes has been diagnosed.

  • glucose_measure: Either "fasting_glucose" or "hba1c".

  • glucose_value: Fasting glucose in mg/dL or HbA1c in percent, as named by glucose_measure. Diagnosed diabetes requires HbA1c. A record with no diabetes diagnosis but a value in the diagnostic diabetes range is rejected because the AHA scoring table does not assign that combination.

  • systolic_bp and diastolic_bp: Blood pressure in mm Hg.

  • antihypertensive_treatment: Whether the blood pressure is treated.

Component input columns may contain missing values or be omitted. A component score is NA_real_ when its available inputs are insufficient. Missing values are never imputed. A warning is emitted when an entire LE8 component cannot be calculated for any observation where AHA defines it.

Pediatric scoring

Rows aged 4 months to 19 years use the children column of Table 1 of the advisory and the suggested rules for younger children in its Supplemental Appendix 2:

  • Diet: MEPA (the adult 16-item screener and adult bands at ages 6-19; a 10-item subset at 10 points per item at ages 2-5; a 6-item subset at ages 6-23 months), or population percentiles at ages 2-19. Not scored before 6 months.

  • Physical activity: daily active play at ages 1-5; weekly moderate or vigorous minutes at ages 6-19. Not scored before 1 year.

  • Nicotine exposure, sleep, BMI, blood lipids, and blood glucose: all pediatric ages, with age-appropriate sleep ranges, growth-chart BMI (weight-for-length or BMI percentile before age 2), and pediatric non-HDL cholesterol bands. Glucose uses the adult table.

  • Blood pressure: AAP 2017 percentile categories at ages 1-12, adult bands at ages 13-19. Not scored before 1 year.

Components AHA does not define at a row's age are NA and are not counted toward min_components; a message notes any such inputs that were supplied. AHA recommends averaging the components that are available and appropriate for measurement in children (the NHANES analysis averaged as few as three), so pediatric analyses usually set a lower min_components. add_pediatric_references() can derive the growth-chart and blood-pressure reference inputs. See vignette("pediatric-scoring").

Where the sources conflict, the package follows the more specific rule: the supplement's 2-5 year diet rule (10 points per item) rather than the Table 1 bands; and, for 6-23 month weight, the supplement's explicit 0-point worst state (at or above the 99.7th percentile with rapid gain) rather than its decrements, which would leave 25. Nineteen-year-olds use the 13-18 year sleep range (8 to 10 hours), the last range AHA lists.

Pediatric input columns

  • smoking_status: "never" (never tried any nicotine product), "former" (tried a nicotine product, but not within 30 days), or "current" (combustible use within 30 days). current_inhaled_nds is inhaled-NDS use within 30 days and caps the score at 25. Record "never" and FALSE for young children without exposure; secondhand_smoke_home applies at every age.

  • active_play_minutes: Ages 1-5. Average daily minutes of active play of any intensity over 7 days.

  • bmi_percentile and bmi_percent_of_p95: Ages 2-19. CDC BMI-for-age percentile (0-100) and BMI as a percentage of the 95th percentile (for example, 125). The latter is used only at or above the 95th percentile. Percentiles below the 5th are rejected because AHA defers to clinician judgment.

  • infant_weight_percentile and infant_weight_z_change: Under age 2. WHO weight-for-length (or BMI-for-age) percentile, and the increase in the matching z-score since the prior routine visit (for example, since age 1 month). The change is required from 6 months; 0.67 or more counts as rapid weight gain.

  • systolic_bp_p90, systolic_bp_p95, diastolic_bp_p90, and diastolic_bp_p95: Ages 1-12. The child's AAP 2017 90th and 95th blood-pressure percentiles in mm Hg for age, sex, and height.

  • MEPA, ages 2-5: ten of the adult items. Vegetables are green_leafy_vegetables + other_vegetables (at least 2 per day) and fruit is berries + other_fruit (at least 14 per week, i.e. 2 per day); whole_grains (3+ per day), olive_oil (1+ per day), fish (1+ per week), nuts (4+ per week), meat (3 or fewer per week), butter_cream (3 or fewer per week), sweets_and_pastries (3 or fewer per week), and fast_food (2 or fewer per month, i.e. at most 24/52 per week). For children under 6, sweets_and_pastries should include sugar-sweetened beverages.

  • MEPA, ages 6-23 months: vegetables and fruit as above (at least 1 per day before 12 months, 2 per day from 12 months), whole_grains (same thresholds), no sweets or sugar-sweetened beverages, no fast food, and milk_source: "human", "cow", "formula", or "other". Human milk meets the item before 12 months; human or cow's milk from 12 months.

Optional clinical-judgment columns

  • apply_lean_muscular_bmi_override: A caller-adjudicated flag asserting that a lean, higher-muscle-mass adult in the general BMI profile has a BMI from 25 to less than 30 and should receive 100 BMI points. If absent, the standard BMI band is used. Not defined for children.

  • apply_sleep_apnea_penalty: If TRUE, subtract 20 points for untreated or undertreated sleep apnea (adults or children). If absent, no discretionary penalty is applied.

  • apply_prediabetes_metformin_penalty: A caller-adjudicated flag asserting that the person has a history of prediabetes, is taking metformin to prevent diabetes, is currently normoglycemic, and the clinician chose to apply the AHA's discretionary 20-point decrement. If absent, no discretionary penalty is applied.

Source-constrained behavior

The function derives the 0-to-16 MEPA total from the 16 raw screener responses. Raw DASH scoring uses the eight-component Fung index: five food groups receive 1 to 5 points by intake quintile; sodium, red/processed meat, and sweetened beverages receive 5 to 1. Intakes equal to a quintile cutpoint stay in the lower quintile. Their sum is dash_total (8 to 40).

Raw HEI-2015 calls compute 13 density, fatty-acid-ratio, and energy-percentage components with proportional scoring between the published standards. Added sugars use 16 kcal per teaspoon equivalent; saturated fat uses 9 kcal per gram. Scores are capped at each component's maximum. Their sum is hei2015_total (0 to 100), which is distinct from the LE8 diet score. With zero saturated fat and positive unsaturated fat, the fatty-acid component receives 10 points; with all three fats zero it receives zero, following the NCI scoring macro. Missing inputs are never treated as zero; a total requires all of its diet components, regardless of min_components.

Raw DASH and HEI-2015 totals are converted to LE8 scores of 0, 25, 50, 80, or 100 using fixed reference total-score cutpoints. Equality enters the higher LE8 band. Explicit cutpoints override the packaged reference and must come from a suitable fixed reference population, using appropriate survey weights and strata where applicable. Cutpoints are never inferred from data. For references requiring different cutpoints by stratum, score strata in separate calls. Alternatively, diet_method = "percentile" accepts externally calculated DASH or HEI-2015 percentiles. The rows in data are never ranked against one another.

The AHA table applies 20-point treatment decrements to blood-lipid and blood-pressure scores. These components are floored at zero, consistent with the AHA's 0-to-100 metric definition. Optional sleep-apnea and prediabetes/metformin decrements are applied only through explicit flags. Inputs are not rounded. The documented MEPA daily/weekly equivalences are applied where the source question and criterion use different timeframes. Combinations without a source-defined score, including simultaneous current combustible smoking and current inhaled-NDS use, produce a structured error.

Input errors inherit from essential8_input_error and essential8_error. General and adult errors also carry essential8_adult_input_error, as in earlier versions; pediatric-only errors carry essential8_pediatric_input_error.

Multiple imputation

With impute, score_le8() fills in missing inputs with mice::mice() several times, scores every completed data set, and returns them stacked. The imputation:

  1. checks the observed values, so data that cannot be scored stop before imputation;

  2. imputes an input only for participants whose age uses it (adult BMI is never imputed for a child, for example), predicting it from age, the other inputs available for the same participants, and any auxiliary columns;

  3. uses predictive mean matching for numeric inputs, so imputed values are always values observed in someone else, and logistic or multinomial regression for categorical inputs;

  4. never imputes a combination the AHA scoring rules do not score, such as diagnosed diabetes without an HbA1c, current smoking with current inhaled-NDS use, or a fasting glucose of 126 mg/dL or more without diagnosed diabetes.

min_components then applies to each completed data set as usual. summary(), dplyr summarise(), and plot() pool the results across imputations with Rubin's rules. See le8_imputation_setup() for the full rules, and to inspect or adjust them.

Imputation assumes values are missing at random given the variables in the imputation models; include the variables used in later analyses, such as exposures and outcomes, with le8_imputation_control(auxiliary = ).

References

Lloyd-Jones DM, Allen NB, Anderson CAM, et al. (2022). Life's Essential 8: Updating and Enhancing the American Heart Association's Construct of Cardiovascular Health. Circulation, 146(5), e18-e43. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001078

Lloyd-Jones DM, Ning H, Labarthe D, et al. (2022). Status of Cardiovascular Health in US Adults and Children Using the American Heart Association's New Life's Essential 8 Metrics. Circulation, 146(11), 822-835. doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.122.060911

Flynn JT, Kaelber DC, Baker-Smith CM, et al. (2017). Clinical Practice Guideline for Screening and Management of High Blood Pressure in Children and Adolescents. Pediatrics, 140(3), e20171904. doi:10.1542/peds.2017-1904

Fung TT, Chiuve SE, McCullough ML, et al. (2008). Adherence to a DASH-Style Diet and Risk of Coronary Heart Disease and Stroke in Women. Archives of Internal Medicine, 168(7), 713-720. doi:10.1001/archinte.168.7.713

Krebs-Smith SM, Pannucci TE, Subar AF, et al. (2018). Update of the Healthy Eating Index: HEI-2015. Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 118(9), 1591-1602. doi:10.1016/j.jand.2018.05.021 See also the National Cancer Institute's scoring standards and algorithm.

See also

summary.essential8_scores(), tidy.essential8_scores(), and plot.essential8_scores() to summarize, reshape, and plot the scores; add_pediatric_references() to derive pediatric growth-chart and blood-pressure inputs; diet_reference() for custom diet references.

Examples

library(dplyr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: ‘dplyr’
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

patient <- tibble(
  id = "patient_1",
  age = 55,
  sex = "female",
  # Daily servings
  olive_oil = 2,
  green_leafy_vegetables = 1,
  other_vegetables = 2,
  whole_grains = 2,
  # Weekly servings
  berries = 3,
  other_fruit = 5,
  meat = 2,
  fish = 3,
  chicken = 2,
  cheese = 1,
  butter_cream = 1,
  beans = 3,
  sweets_and_pastries = 1,
  nuts = 4,
  alcohol = 4,
  # Fast-food meals per week
  fast_food = 0,
  moderate_activity_minutes = 90,
  vigorous_activity_minutes = 0,
  smoking_status = "former",
  years_since_quit = 6,
  current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = FALSE,
  sleep_hours = 7.5,
  bmi = 27.5,
  bmi_profile = "general",
  non_hdl_cholesterol = 145,
  lipid_lowering_treatment = FALSE,
  diabetes = FALSE,
  glucose_measure = "fasting_glucose",
  glucose_value = 95,
  systolic_bp = 128,
  diastolic_bp = 78,
  antihypertensive_treatment = FALSE
)

scores <- score_le8(patient, diet_method = "mepa")
select(scores, id, mepa_total, diet_score, le8_composite_score,
       le8_category)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   id        mepa_total diet_score le8_composite_score le8_category
#>   <chr>          <int>      <dbl>               <dbl> <chr>       
#> 1 patient_1         14         80                  80 high        

# A 4-year-old with the preschool diet screener and no laboratory values.
child <- tibble(
  id = "child_1",
  age = 4,
  # Ten MEPA items apply at ages 2-5; sweets include sugary drinks.
  green_leafy_vegetables = 1, other_vegetables = 1, # servings per day
  berries = 7, other_fruit = 14,                     # servings per week
  whole_grains = 2, olive_oil = 1,                   # servings per day
  sweets_and_pastries = 2, meat = 2, fish = 1,       # servings per week
  nuts = 2, butter_cream = 1,
  fast_food = 0.25,                                  # times per week
  active_play_minutes = 160,
  smoking_status = "never", current_inhaled_nds = FALSE,
  secondhand_smoke_home = FALSE,
  sleep_hours = 11,
  bmi_percentile = 60, bmi_percent_of_p95 = 85,
  systolic_bp = 98, diastolic_bp = 58,
  systolic_bp_p90 = 103, systolic_bp_p95 = 107,
  diastolic_bp_p90 = 63, diastolic_bp_p95 = 67,
  antihypertensive_treatment = FALSE
)

child_scores <- score_le8(child, min_components = 5)
#> Warning: ! Some LE8 components could not be calculated for any observations.
#> ✖ Blood lipids
#> ✖ Blood glucose
#> ℹ Overall LE8 composite scores will use the available components, subject to
#>   `min_components`.
select(child_scores, id, mepa_total, ends_with("_score"), n_components)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 12
#>   id     mepa_total diet_score physical_activity_sc…¹ nicotine_score sleep_score
#>   <chr>       <int>      <dbl>                  <dbl>          <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 child…          8         80                     90            100         100
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​physical_activity_score
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: bmi_score <dbl>, blood_lipids_score <dbl>,
#> #   blood_glucose_score <dbl>, blood_pressure_score <dbl>,
#> #   le8_composite_score <dbl>, n_components <int>

# Multiply impute missing inputs, then pool the scores.
adults <- read.csv(system.file(
  "extdata", "le8-adult-example.csv", package = "essential8"
))
adults <- adults[!startsWith(names(adults), "expected_")]
adults$non_hdl_cholesterol[c(2, 5)] <- NA

imputed <- score_le8(adults, impute = le8_imputation_control(m = 5, seed = 1))
#> Warning: Number of logged events: 55
summary(imputed)
#> LE8 scores: 10 participants (10 adult), pooled over 5 imputations
#> Diet method: mepa; min_components: 7
#> Composite score available for 10 of 10 (average over imputations).
#> 
#>                    n mean    95% CI  fmi   sd median
#> LE8 composite     10 48.4 27.2-69.5 0.19 28.6   49.1

#> Nicotine exposure 10 40.0 15.4-64.6 0.19 33.3   30.0
#> Sleep             10 55.0 28.5-81.5 0.19 36.0   55.0
#> BMI               10 46.5 20.2-72.8 0.19 35.7   50.0
#> Blood lipids      10 46.4 17.9-74.9 0.31 34.9   42.0
#> Blood glucose     10 46.0 22.6-69.4 0.19 31.7   50.0
#> Blood pressure    10 42.0 19.4-64.6 0.19 30.7   40.0
#> Means pooled with Rubin's rules; fmi = fraction of missing information.
#> 
#> Category (rows with a composite score):
#>            n percent    95% CI
#>   low      5   50.0% 13.1-86.9
